expected_verdict: POOL fetch-07-1591626a, 4 files, 40 rows, exit 0 — and the census reports status with 8 distinct values where the shape was written for 2
phenomenon: The hole the stamp does not close. These four ledgers share ONE derived stamp and pool cleanly, so the gate says yes. Their `status` column nevertheless holds eight distinct values: OK, FAIL, NOT-REACHED, SEARCH, REDIR, PARTIAL, SUMMARISED, SEARCH-COUNT. Every straggler comes from c991/c992/c993, the three most recent files — the header froze 21 cycles ago and the meaning kept moving underneath it. tools/fetchledger.py refuses exactly those three by name (VALUE-OUTSIDE-DECLARED-VOCABULARY); this tool admits them. The case exists to keep that asymmetry executable: a stamp derived from a header covers COLUMN drift and is blind to VOCABULARY drift, which is the drift that actually happened to me.
